diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $(\lambda,\mathbf{u}, p)$ and $(\lambda_{h},\mathbf{u}_{h}, p_{h})$ be the $j$th eigenpair of (\ref{s2.2})-(\ref{s2.3})

issues.failure_explanation: The proof reduces the desired bound to the identity bracket $=(\lambda_h-\lambda)(\mathbf{u}_h,\mathbf{v}_h)$ and then divides by $|(\mathbf{u}_h,\mathbf{v}_h)|$, invoking a lower bound 'uniformly with respect to h' borrowed from Wang2024. For a defective eigenvalue the right eigenfunction and the adjoint eigenfunction are L2-orthogonal (Jordan-block structure: (u,u*)=0), so (u_h,u_h^*) -> 0 and no h-uniform lower bound exists; the lemma states no non-defectiveness hypothesis. Since Theorem th3-8 uses exactly this lemma (with [v_h,q_h]=[u_h^*,p_h^*]) without any non-defectiveness assumption, its bound is unestablished there; in fact for a defective eigenvalue |lambda-lambda_h| is O(||T-T_h||^{1/2}) while eta_h = O(||T-T_h||^{1/2}), so a bound of the type (s3.33) cannot hold.

failure_location.quote: Applying the same argument as in Lemma 5 in \cite{Wang2024}, we deduce that $|(\mathbf{u}_{h},\mathbf{v}_{h})|$ has a positive lower bound uniformly with respect to $h$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Lemma lem3-7 and Theorem th3-8 to non-defective, biorthogonally normalized eigenpairs (as the paper's own cluster corollary cor:added-1 already does); for defective eigenvalues no bound of type (s3.33) is supported by the source.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenpair relation (s2.78) and the a posteriori eigenvalue reliability bound (s3.33) of Theorem th3-8 are unestablished (and (s3.33) is false) for defective eigenvalues; the eigenfunction reliability/effectiveness results are untouched since they do not use this step.
issues.title: Uniform lower bound for the eigenpairing fails for defective eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: The supported resolution is a contained hypothesis restriction: with the non-defectiveness assumption (already used elsewhere in the paper) the identity and the eigenvalue estimator retain their guarantees, so a recognizably comparable result survives; no new proof architecture is needed, but the advertised eigenvalue guarantee is narrowed.

issues.failure_explanation: By the adjoint consistency (s2.62) with f = u_i^*, ((T-T_h)u_j, u_i^*) = A_h(w, T*u_i^*) + conj(B_h(w, S*u_i^*)). Splitting T*u_i^* = I_h T*u_i^* + error and S*u_i^* = vartheta_h S*u_i^* + error, the term with vartheta_h vanishes only via the discrete adjoint equation, and A_h(w, I_hT*u_i^*) must be evaluated with the primal DG error equation, giving -B_h(I_hT*u_i^*, Su_j - S_hu_j). The displayed middle term B_h(T*u_i^* - I_hT*u_i^*, S*u_i^* - S_h^*u_i^*) does not follow from any identity in the source (it pairs the adjoint interpolation error with the adjoint pressure error), and the first term even carries the wrong index (T*u_j^* instead of T*u_i^*). Moreover, bounding the correct remainder at rate h^{2s} requires div(I_h T*u_i^*) = O(h^s) (divergence-free T*u_i^* plus an H^1-interpolation estimate), an argument absent from the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the decomposition: after splitting the second argument, evaluate A_h(w, I_h T^*u_i^*) with the primal DG error equation A_h(w, v_h) = -B_h(v_h, Su_j - S_hu_j), and bound -B_h(I_hT^*u_i^*, Su_j - S_hu_j) via div(I_h T^*u_i^*) = div(T*u_i^* - I_hT*u_i^*) = O(h^s) together with the pressure error estimate, yielding the stated O(h^{2s}).
issues.overall_effect: The cluster-mean eigenvalue rate (s2.80) of Theorem th2-7 (the possibly defective case) is not established by the given proof; the other estimates of the theorem rely on different arguments.
issues.title: Invalid identity in the proof of the cluster eigenvalue rate (th2-7)
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained (one re-derived identity plus a standard superapproximation step already implicit in the cited tools); the conclusion (s2.80) survives with the same rate, so the loss is limited and the argument is contained but nontrivial.

issues.failure_explanation: The substitution inserts the estimates (s3.12)-(s3.13), whose right-hand sides contain the l1-type sums sum_tau (eta_R_tau + eta_F_tau + eta_J_tau) and sum_tau ||div u_h||_{0,tau} multiplied by GLOBAL norms. In the supremum of (s3.8) these sums cannot be dominated by the global estimator eta_h uniformly in h: sum_tau eta_tau <= sqrt(N) eta_h with N the number of elements, which grows as h -> 0. Hence the proof does not establish (s3.22)-(s3.23) with h-independent constants. The intermediate estimate (s3.15) in the proof of Lemma le3-2 already has the local (l2/patch-weighted) form needed, so the gap is in the formulation of (s3.12)-(s3.13) and its use in th3-4.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State Lemma le3-2 with local weights (eta_R_tau, eta_F_tau against ||nabla v||_{0,theta_tau}-type local norms and ||div u_h||_{0,tau}||q||_{0,theta_tau}, as already obtained in (s3.15)-(s3.16)) and apply Cauchy-Schwarz with the bounded-overlap of the patches; then Theorem th3-4 follows with h-independent constants.
issues.overall_effect: The reliability bounds (s3.22)-(s3.23), the eigenvalue bound (s3.33) built on them, and the equivalences of Corollary cor:added-1 are not established with h-independent constants by the written argument; the adaptive Algorithm 1's marking justification is affected.
issues.title: Reliability proof of th3-4 leaves mesh-dependent (sqrt N) constants
issues.why_classification: The repair is a routine localization of estimates whose local versions are already derived inside the source; every advertised rate, guarantee, and the adaptive algorithm survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By using $[\![\mathbf{u}]\!]=0$ for any $F\in \mathcal{E}_{h}^{i}$, and $\mathbf{u}=0 $ for any $F\subset\partial\Omega$, we get (\ref{s3.26}).

issues.failure_explanation: For vector fields the source defines [![v]] as the scalar normal jump, whereas eta_{J_tau} is defined with the full tensor jump [![\underline{u_h}]] (Frobenius norm equal to ||u_h^+ - u_h^-||_{0,F}) and the full boundary trace ||u_h \otimes n||_{0,F} = ||u_h||_{0,F}. The asserted equalities (s3.26) and (s3.29) therefore keep only the normal components and are false whenever u_h has a nonzero tangential jump (interior faces) or nonzero tangential boundary trace; the proof step ([![u]]=0 for interior faces, u=0 on the boundary) supports only the version with the full tensor jumps.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |[![u_h-u]]|^2 by ||[![\underline{u_h-u}]]||^2 and ||(u_h-u)\cdot n||^2 by ||(u_h-u)\otimes n||^2 in (s3.26) and (s3.29); the proof's justification ([![u]] = 0, u = 0 on the boundary) then applies verbatim and all efficiency statements hold.
issues.overall_effect: The efficiency identities (s3.26)/(s3.29) of Lemma lem3-5 are false as written, so the efficiency theorem th3-6 (which is derived from them) and the equivalences in Corollary cor:added-1 that rely on the tangential part of eta_J are not supported as written.
issues.title: False jump identity in the efficiency estimates (eta_J in lem3-5)
issues.why_classification: A purely notational correction of the two displayed identities; the bubble-function argument in the proof is exactly the tensor version, so no inference, rate, or guarantee needs to change.
